tradition: Western historical physiognomy — Lavater/Hunter Volume I documentary scope
orientation_convention: Software annotation convention,not a Lavater formula: view left_profile means anatomical left side visible. Subject-side labels remain anatomical; frontal viewer labels swap under nonmirrored display and agree under mirrored display. Unknown mirroring remains ambiguous. Profile viewer labels cannot determine anatomical side.

regions.region_definition: Forehead down to the eyebrows,as the author explicitly bounds it.

historical_reference.region_description: Forehead down to the eyebrows,as the author explicitly bounds it.
historical_reference.historical_association: In Fragment II,Lavater assigned the forehead to his category 'intellectual life'. This is a historical assertion,not evidence about any observed person.
historical_reference.limitations: Region-only documentary lookup. Geometry,markings,side and proportions do not select a personal interpretation; the author's intelligence/morality/animal-life claims are not operationalized.

source_example.orientation: Abstract forehead/quadrant schematic,not a frontal face or anatomical left/right claim.
source_example.historical_context: Lavater used these constructions to argue for ranking intellectual capacity from skull/forehead proportions. That discredited inference is documented here,not calculated or applied to a person.

terminology.description: Hunter's translation uses physiognomy for the proposed science and physionomy for outward appearance; this records terminology,not scientific endorsement.
Lavater contrasted fixed/resting form with features in motion,calling the latter pathognomy. No emotion,character or internal state is inferred by this engine.

limits: Historical/symbolic reference only. Physiognomic claims about character or ability are discredited.
Historical associations are selected by region only,never by observed geometry,markings,measurements or side.
Normalized points and side labels are manual annotations; no image processing or anatomical landmark detection.
Observer accuracy and source fidelity are different questions; schematic transcriptions do not validate real-person judgments.
Chinese Mian Xiang,five elements and12 palaces remain unsupported and are not merged with Lavater.
Only the inspected Hunter1789 Volume I pages/figures are covered; no Holcroft/other-volume substitution.
